verses.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, masons, and carpenters to build him a palace.
David realized that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had made his kingdom great for the sake of his people Israel.
David married more wives in Jerusalem and had more sons and daughters.
These were the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all went up to look for him. David heard about it and went out to meet them.
The Philistines had come and raided the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked God, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?” The LORD said, “Go. I'll hand them over to you.”

David and his men went up to Baal Perazim and defeated them there. David said, “God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like water breaking through a barrier.” So they named that place Baal Perazim.
The Philistines left their gods behind. David ordered them burned.
The Philistines raided the valley again.
David asked God what to do again. God said, “Don't go straight up after them. Circle around and approach them from opposite the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the treetops, go out to fight. God will have gone ahead of you to strike the Philistine army.”
David did what God commanded, and his men struck down the Philistine army from Gibeon as far as Gezer.
David's fame spread to every land, and the LORD made all the nations fear him.
